clue.text: A topping craftsman!

parts.note: a 'topping' here is a hat, something worn on top of the head, so the craftsman is the one who makes hats rather than a first-rate worker

explanation.surface: Praise for a splendid craftsman, 'topping' in the old British slang sense of excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat-maker makes headwear, the topping a person puts on.

clue.text: Beautiful homes-and otherwise!

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that houses are lovely, and more besides.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-looking is the meaning shared by both words.

clue.text: Without ups and downs in the main

definitions.text: Without ups and downs in the main

parts.words: Without ups and downs in the main
parts.note: 'in the main' seems to mean mostly, but the main is the sea, whose ups and downs are the rise and fall of its waters

explanation.surface: A life that is mostly even and uneventful.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea with no rising and falling water lacks a tidal flow.

clue.text: The Spanish quarter is different

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
SE, south-east, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A city's Spanish district is unlike the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Other or besides means something different.

clue.text: Just a few words might be fine

explanation.surface: A remark that a short message might be acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit is a short run of words; a court's penalty, which may be a monetary fine, is also called this.

clue.text: Getting in for nothing, using charm-clear?

parts.note: to entrance is to charm or enchant
free means clear, as in clear of obstacles

explanation.surface: Sneaking in without paying by charming the doorman and having a clear run.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission without charge means no fee to get in.

clue.text: Sort the letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind or variety is a sort; printed characters are also this.

clue.text: In days gone by one ate royally in rather more elegant fashion

annotationWithheld.why: In days gone by one ate royally in rather more elegant fashion (6): NEATER fits 'rather more elegant', but no parse of 'In days gone by one ate royally' giving the letters N, E, A, T, E, R could be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: In days gone by one ate royally in rather more elegant fashion

clue.text: One and one don't make two!

definitions.text: One and one don't make two!

parts.words: One and one don't make two!
parts.note: written as figures side by side, a 1 next to a 1 reads as a two-digit number, not a sum

explanation.surface: A denial of the simplest arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The digits 1 and 1 written together give the number after ten.

clue.text: He's barely ready to face life

definitions.text: He's barely ready to face life

parts.words: He's barely ready to face life
parts.note: 'barely' read literally means wearing nothing, so the person faces the world unclothed

explanation.surface: A young man scarcely prepared for the challenges of adulthood.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about without clothes, literally bare.

clue.text: An end to double parking will be accepted by the wise

indicators.note: being accepted by something means being taken inside it, so these words place one piece within another

parts.note: a sage is a wise person
taken as written

indicators.note: double asks for the parking abbreviation to be written twice

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Wise folk will welcome a ban on double parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' writes P twice; TO and PP together go inside SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt or cessation is a stopping, the end of an activity.

clue.text: Looks into building at given sites

indicators.note: building means constructing something new from the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An inspector examining construction work at certain locations.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ATGIVENSITES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine or inquire into something is to probe it.

clue.text: There's only fish

explanation.surface: A statement that there is nothing but fish on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or exclusive, and is also a flatfish.

clue.text: Running round, pant badly

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the following word are put together wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A jogger going round the track and panting hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges PANT to NTAP, after O. 'Running' here means flowing from a tap, as beer from a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer that is available to draw from the barrel is flowing, running from the tap.

clue.text: A divine waitress!

parts.note: 'divine' is not praise but literal: a goddess who served drinks to the gods of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Praise for a delightful waitress.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the goddess of youth was cupbearer to the Olympians.

clue.text: A note to deliver bitter

parts.note: C is a musical note
to rid is to deliver or free

explanation.surface: A bitter note that must be delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, pungent taste or smell is harsh and unpleasant.

clue.text: Listened to the sound of the cattle

indicators.note: the sound of says the answer is pronounced like the word given by what follows

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle

explanation.surface: Someone attentive to the lowing of cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one has listened to has been perceived by ear.

clue.text: A tutor's tie-much care's needed here

indicators.note: these words ask for the letters of the phrase before them to be arranged into what is wanted here

explanation.surface: Advice that a teacher must take great care over the neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TIEMUCHCARES are rearranged; the 's after 'tutor' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano or violin instructor is a tutor in that art.

clue.text: Respectful always in the break

indicators.note: in places the word for always inside the word for the break

parts.note: a rent is a break or tear
ever means always

explanation.surface: Being consistently polite during an interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deep respect is being devout or reverential.

clue.text: Get the fool to come in-he's quite agreeable

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to enter is to come in

explanation.surface: Letting a fool inside who turns out to be pleasant company.
explanation.definitionFit: One who consents is willing to go along with a proposal.

clue.text: Members of the upper classes

parts.note: not the aristocracy but pupils in the highest classes of a British secondary school

explanation.surface: A description of aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools the final two years (ages 16 to 18) are called the sixth form.
explanation.definitionFit: Students in the senior years of a school are in its top classes.

clue.text: Ecclesiastic circle, this may be

indicators.note: says the word before may become the answer when its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ring of churchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is a man of the church.

clue.text: Fifty over-five hundred over-that's capital!

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
on means over, as in a lid on a box
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
on means over, as before

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer counting overs and runs and exclaiming in delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital!' is also an old British exclamation meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The English and UK seat of government is a capital city.

clue.text: The beast left one with no come-back

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a come-back here is a return, so the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: An animal abandoned with no way to return.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is the archetypal wild animal, king of the jungle.

clue.text: Fit to get about in time

indicators.note: in places the word for about inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Getting fit takes some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that tally or correspond are said to suit each other.

clue.text: Some pose real problems when dried up

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Drought causes real difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere describes vegetation that is withered and parched.

clue.text: Figure on entering the Church

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A notable person joining the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid shape with a circular base and a point is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Courageous creatures?

explanation.surface: A question about brave animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky means brave; animals hunted for sport are also so called.

clue.text: Old soldiers scared to get involved

indicators.note: letters that get involved are mixed up together, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Veterans frightened of taking part in a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAREDTO rearranged; British soldiers once wore scarlet tunics.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic British infantry were nicknamed for their scarlet uniforms.

clue.text: It could be a mother and father split

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: A couple, mother and father, who might be separating.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is one example of someone who raises a child.

clue.text: Talk, being contrary

explanation.surface: Someone arguing for the sake of being awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to hold conversation; as a noun or adjective the word means the opposite.

clue.text: Trouble caused by nobleman imprisoning holy man

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman
ST is short for saint

explanation.surface: A noble who has jailed a priest causes difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone persistently is to give them bother.
